sentences.text: This creature had a tadpole-shaped body completely covered in dermal denticles and featured an enlarged abdomen.
The originally described fetal specimens measured 35 mm and 29 mm in length.
Evidence of sharp teeth and fecal matter suggests that Delphyodontos practiced intrauterine cannibalism.
The adult form of Delphyodontos is unknown because fossils consist only of aborted fetuses or recently born young.
Delphyodontos dacriformes is a basal cartilaginous fish found in the Late Mississippian Bear Gulch Limestone of Montana.
The genus name Delphyodontos means "womb tooth".
Delphyodontos was viviparous, meaning it gave birth to live young rather than laying eggs.
Delphyodontos inhabited a shallow marine bay of tropical waters represented by the Bear Gulch Limestone.
Delphyodontos was a benthic animal with a range extending from the bay mouth to the reef and upper basin.
A 2009 phylogeny found Delphyodontos to be related to the undescribed chondrichthyan ElWeir.
Delphyodontos lived during the Serpukhovian, between 326.9 and 323.6 million years ago.
